record.original_question: Let X be an Enriques surface and let Ku(X, L) be the Kuznetsov component determined by a collection L of exceptional line bundles in a semiorthogonal decomposition Db(X) = <Ku(X, L), L>. Is Ku(X, L) indecomposable?

evidence.quote: Thus, if X is an Enriques surface and L is a collection of exceptional line bundles as in Proposition 2.7, then we get a semiorthogonal decomposition Db (X) = hKu(X, L), Li.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $D^b(X)$ denote its bounded derived category of coherent sheaves. Suppose $\mathcal{L} = (L_1, \ldots, L_n)$ is an exceptional collection of line bundles on $X$ (i.e., each $L_i$ satisfies $\mathrm{Ext}^k(L_i,L_i) = 0$ for $k \neq 0$ and $\mathrm{Ext}^k(L_i,L_j) = 0$ for $i > j$ and all $k$) such that there is a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathrm{Ku}(X, \mathcal{L}),\, L_1, \ldots, L_n \rangle,$$
where $\mathrm{Ku}(X, \mathcal{L})$ — the Kuznetsov component — is the right orthogonal to $\langle L_1, \ldots, L_n \rangle$ in $D^b(X)$.

Determine whether $\mathrm{Ku}(X, \mathcal{L})$ is always indecomposable as a triangulated category, i.e., whether it admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2022 survey on categorical Torelli theorems lists this exact question as an open problem (Question 3.9(ii)), noting that a positive answer would yield a counterexample to the Jordan–Hölder property for semiorthogonal decompositions and would have implications for the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on Ku(X,L). No resolution is reported in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Question 3.9(ii): Is Ku(X,L) indecomposable? ... would yield another counterexample to the Jordan–Hölder property for semiorthogonal decompositions.
status_evidence.claim: The indecomposability of Ku(X,L) for an Enriques surface is listed as an open problem in a 2022 survey.
